newsitem.title: USA: AM International Inc Q1 profit vs loss.
newsitem.headline: AM International Inc Q1 profit vs loss.

text.p: AM International Inc said Wednesday earnings for its fiscal first quarter ended November 2, 1996 totaled $500,000 or $0.07 a share compared with a loss before results of discontinued operations of $3.5 million or $0.49 for the comparable prior year quarter.

The business of AM International now consists of AM Multigraphics business, which distributes pre-press equipment and supplies and provides technical services to the graphics arts industry. The business currently employs about 800 people.
AM International has previously announced the sale of substantially all of the assets of its Sheridan Systems Division and the sale of its interest in AM Japan Co Ltd.

In its fiscal year ended July 31, 1996, the company also completed the divestitures of its unprofitable European subsidiaries and in October 1996 the company's Canadian subsidiary filed a voluntary assignment in bankruptcy.
AM has also announced its exit from the manufacture and distribution of offset duplicating presses and post press equipment used in the graphics arts market.
During the first quarter, the company began to sell off press and post press inventories.

Revenues for its first quarter of $27.7 million were $15.3 million below the prior year comparative quarter. Revenues of divested foreign subsidiaries in Japan and Canada accounted for $6.8 million of the decrease and the sell-off of press and post press equipment accounted for a decrease of $5.3 million.

Gross margin decreased by $3.6 million due to the divestitures of foreign subsidiaries and lower revenue levels, particularly in press and post press product lines. Selling, general and administrative expenses fell by $5.5 million due to cost cutting actions taken as part of the reorganization.
AM also had a $2.1 million gain in the quarter primarily from divestiture of the company's interest in AM Japan Co Ltd.

In October, AM agreed to merge with a corporation newly formed by affiliates of Pacholder Associates Inc, a Cincinnati-based investment manager and advisor. The proposed transaction requires certain conditions including approval by a majority of AM's shareholders at a meeting which is tentatively scheduled for February 1997.
